topic: The $9,250 Louis XIII pizza from Salerno (Part 2)
style: Photorealistic luxury food look, dark and rich with gold accents
requestedEnding: Asks the viewer whether they would pay it, then promises part three

storyArc.protagonist: A tiny pizza with lobster and three caviars
storyArc.setting: dark luxury restaurant counters and an Italian wood oven
storyArc.goal: Show the pizza that costs over three times the record pizza from Part 1.
storyArc.obstacle: Why does a pizza under eight inches cost about $9,250?
storyArc.turn: Lobster, three caviars, 72-hour dough, and Louis XIII cognac with Krug champagne.
storyArc.visualBible: Dark marble, candlelight, gold and amber accents, photorealistic food photography, no people faces.

plan.title: Part 2: The $9,250 Pizza vs the $2,700 Pizza
plan.hook: This pizza costs over nine thousand dollars, yet feeds only two.
plan.payoff: Would you pay nine thousand dollars for pizza? Follow for part three!
claimsToCheck: Tasting Table: Louis XIII pizza by Renato Viola, Salerno, EUR 8,300 (about $9,250), under eight inches, serves two; three types of rare caviar, fresh lobster, prawns, buffalo mozzarella; dough proofed 72 hours; served with Remy Martin Louis XIII cognac and Krug Clos du Mesnil 1995 champagne (tastingtable.com/749277/this-is-the-most-expensive-pizza-in-the-world). Checked 9 Nov 2026
Guinness World Records: $2,700 Industry Kitchen pizza, 24 April 2017 (from Part 1, already verified)
